raw_response:
I'm a 44-year-old woman, farming these 5 mu in Quzhou for 20 years now. My husband works at a construction site in Handan — he only comes back for planting and harvest. My mother-in-law lives with us and helps when she can, spreading fertilizer or watching the pump. My daughter is in middle school and my son is in high school, so they only help during summer holiday. Mostly it's me and the old lady handling the farm.

The wheat I planted last October is standing okay. I bought "Jimai" improved seed last year and saved the big grains — cost me about 30 yuan per mu for the seed and dressing medicine. Before planting, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu and plowed it in, same as we always do. Now it's spring, and I already topdressed two weeks ago when I saw Old Zhang's wife doing hers. I put about 30 jin of urea per mu — that's about 15 kg. Some people say 20 jin is enough, but last year I tried less and the wheat looked yellow. Better to put a bit more. I don't want to risk losing yield. Fertilizer prices went up again at the shop, so I only bought what I needed: two big bags for the wheat topdress, and I'll get one more for the maize later.

For water, I irrigated the wheat once before winter, and I just irrigated again at jointing in late March. I'll irrigate one more time before heading if it stays dry. Pumping costs electricity — every time I turn on the well pump, the meter spins fast. Three times for wheat is enough. My neighbor with the bigger farm irrigates four times, but he has more money than me.

Wheat harvest is early June. I hire the combine for 50 yuan per mu — my nephew drives it. Then I have to get the maize in quick, within two or three days, or the season gets too short and the frost comes early. I buy hybrid maize seed from the agricultural shop, the yellow bag — "Zhengdan" something. It's 48 yuan per mu. Everyone knows you can't save maize seed, it doesn't work the second year.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow — about 40 jin per mu. Then at the big喇叭口 stage in July, if the leaves look light green, I topdress with urea, about 25 jin per mu. If the color looks fine, maybe I skip it to save money for my son's school fees. Last year I skipped and still got decent yield, so I'll see.

Maize irrigation — probably twice. Once at jointing, and once at flowering if July is dry. I'm hoping for rain because pumping is expensive and we need cash in hand for emergencies. I don't spray insecticide unless I see worms. For weeds, I spray atrazine on the maize right after planting, before the seedlings come up. For the wheat, I already did one herbicide spray this spring when I saw too many shepherd's purse in the field.

Labor is mostly family — me and my mother-in-law. She can spread fertilizer and watch the water, but she can't do heavy work. I hire two days for wheat harvest and two days for maize harvest. Planting the maize after wheat, I do by hand myself — I can plant one mu a day if I hurry, no time to wait for a machine.

I expect about 400 kg per mu for wheat, and maybe 450 kg for maize if the weather holds. That's what I usually get. I don't aim for the highest yield in the village — I aim for not losing money and having enough grain for the family. Total costs this year — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, electricity for water, hired labor — I figure about 2,900 yuan. That's a lot for us, but we have to do it.
